0: Khlestakov and Luka Lukich, who is practically pushed in on the stage. A voice behind him is heard saying nearly aloud, "Don't be chickenhearted." LUKA [drawing himself up, trembling, with his hand on his sword]. I have the honor to present myself—School Inspector, Titular Councilor Khlopov.
1: KHLESTAKOV. I'm glad to see you. Take a seat, take a seat. Will you have a cigar? [Offers him a cigar.]
2: LUKA [to himself, hesitating]. There now! That's something I hadn't anticipated. To take or not to take?
3: KHLESTAKOV. Take it, take it. It's a pretty good cigar. Of course not what you get in St. Petersburg. There I used to smoke twenty-five cent cigars. You feel like kissing yourself after having smoked one of them. Here, light it. [Hands him a candle.]
4: Luka Lukich tries to light the cigar shaking all over.
5: KHLESTAKOV. Not that end, the other.
6: LUKA [drops the cigar from fright, spits and shakes his hands. Aside]. Confound it! My damned timidity has ruined me!
7: KHLESTAKOV. I see you are not a lover of cigars. I confess smoking is my weakness—smoking and the fair sex. Not for the life of me can I remain indifferent to the fair sex. How about you? Which do you like more, brunettes or blondes?
8: Luka Lukich remains silent, at a complete loss what to say.
9: KHLESTAKOV. Tell me frankly, brunettes or blondes?
10: LUKA. I don't dare to know.
11: KHLESTAKOV. No, no, don't evade. I'm bound to know your taste.
12: LUKA. I venture to report to you—[Aside.] I don't know what I'm saying.
13: KHLESTAKOV. Ah, you don't want to say. I suppose some little brunette or other has cast a spell over you. Confess, she has, hasn't she?
15: KHLESTAKOV. Ah, you're blushing. You see. Why don't you speak?
16: LUKA. I'm scared, your Hon—High—Ex—[Aside.] Done for! My confounded tongue has undone me!
17: KHLESTAKOV. You're scared? There IS something awe-inspiring in my eyes, isn't there? At least I know not a single woman can resist them. Isn't that so?
19: KHLESTAKOV. A strange thing happened to me on the road. I ran entirely out of cash. Can you lend me three hundred rubles?
20: LUKA [clutching his pockets. Aside]. A fine business if I haven't got the money! I have! I have! [Takes out the bills and gives them to him, trembling.]
22: LUKA [drawing himself up, with his hand on his sword]. I will not venture to disturb you with my presence any longer.
24: LUKA [dashes out almost at a run, saying aside.] Well, thank the Lord! Maybe he won't inspect the schools.
